news.title: Oil prices dip over 6% after US, Iran pause fighting over weekend
news.summary:
STORY: Oil prices fell more than 6% at one stage on Monday.

The relief came after the U.S. and Iran paused strikes over the weekend following two weeks of attacks.

The latest move raised hopes of a diplomatic solution to de-escalate the conflict and allow shipping to resume in the key Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude future fell more than $6 to a touch over $90, though later slightly rose.

U.S. West Texas Intermediate was also down just under $6 at around $83 a barrel, but also marginally rose later.

Both contracts are trading at their lowest levels in nearly a week after rising for the past three weeks.

The U.S. Iran conflict has lowered oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

It has lately spilled over to the Red Sea and hit exports from the world's top exporter Saudi Arabia via the Bab el-Mandeb strait to Asia.

The latest developments sent Brent to $100 per barrel.

The U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, Mike Waltz, gave an update to U.S. media over the weekend on Iran.

He said President Trump had decided to pause U.S. attacks to allow more time for diplomacy.

However, ship traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb strait fell on Sunday.

That after Yemeni Houthis attacked Saudi oil installations along the Red Sea coast.
